searchText: Hey all, I was looking to clarify few scenarios related to `dataColumnSidecars` which I found not fully clarified in the specs. Want to know how other client teams handles those scenarios: Scenario 1: Peer requested for a data column for which we don't have custody Scenario 2: Peer requested for a data column for block which have zero blobs Scenario 3: Peer requested for a data column which we should have custody but we dont have it (in our db) My understanding is following: Scenario 1: Abort the request with `invalid_request` error Scenario 2: Just skip those columns and not respond anything Scenario 3: Abort the request with `resource_unavailable` How you guys are handling these scenarios? <@&595681804422479873> <@&595683609080365088> <@&836981489430036500> <@&595683849225240704> Currently, when a peer requests some data column sidecars, Prysm responds with what it has, regardless it effectively advertises the requested sidecars. So, in both scenarios 1, 2 and 3, it will not respond anything and close the stream. And, on the contrary, if Prysm advertises columns 1, 2, 3 for a given root, but, for some reason, also has column 4 in DB, and a peers requests column 4, then it will respond with column 4. (without downscoring the peer) Client devs, thoughts on this PR? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4542 I was reading it today, in principle I have nothing against it. We won't use it at all I assume, but I also don't like it when the spec leaks, so I think this will be such a case where the spec won't leak to clients. Thanks for the feedback, interesting. How does Prysm plan to implement this? Sort of like how the spec currently is? <@680234424037670912> I know you started working on this. Would this PR be helpful for Teku? Oh you've already commented, thanks! We had a slightly different approach. With more semantic names for the functions. yeah, it's kinda hard for me to tell you right now, I suspect there's going to be some inertia to move from our current design around timings. Nice, yeah I like the approach described in the comment. <@680234424037670912> what does "so i think its worth having that in the interface" mean exactly? We could add `get_attestation_due_ms()` style helper functions. That sounds reasonable. I'm not sure if I should speak for Paul, but my understanding is that he meant that it is worth having those methods for each duration instead of a single method that receives the duration_id. Got it, yes that was my understanding as well. When I get back from PTO, I will make an alternative PR which does it that way. If <@555483069038198827> thinks that's a good compromise. basically yep we wanted to just be able to call a function at a slot and get the expected duration for a specific thing (attestation due, aggregation due, slot duration etc) +1 this is what I had in mind on how we would implement this

excerpts.author: nazarhussain
excerpts.content:
Hey all, I was looking to clarify few scenarios related to `dataColumnSidecars` which I found not fully clarified in the specs. Want to know how other client teams handles those scenarios: 

Scenario 1: Peer requested for a data column for which we don't have custody 
Scenario 2: Peer requested for a data column for block which have zero blobs 
Scenario 3: Peer requested for a data column which we should have custody but we dont have it (in our db)

My understanding is following: 

Scenario 1: Abort the request with `invalid_request` error 
Scenario 2: Just skip those columns and not respond anything 
Scenario 3: Abort the request with `resource_unavailable` 

How you guys are handling these scenarios? <@&595681804422479873> <@&595683609080365088> <@&836981489430036500> <@&595683849225240704>

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content: Currently, when a peer requests some data column sidecars, Prysm responds with what it has, regardless it effectively advertises the requested sidecars. So, in both scenarios 1, 2 and 3, it will not respond anything and close the stream.

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content: And, on the contrary, if Prysm advertises columns 1, 2, 3 for a given root, but, for some reason, also has column 4 in DB, and a peers requests column 4, then it will respond with column 4.
